THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: A competitive firm's short-run supply curve is the rising portion of marginal cost at and above minimum average variable cost. The tax is tied to each unit produced. MC gives the additional cost of supply. The short-run supply schedule depends on marginal and variable costs, not fixed cost.

WATCH OUT

runs.text: Do not assume fixed cost shifts supply. The short-run supply schedule depends on marginal and variable costs, not fixed cost. Fixed cost affects profit but not the short-run MC-above-AVC supply schedule.

transcript.sourceText: The firm's short-run supply curve is the portion of MC at and above minimum AVC, which begins at point A: 22 units and $20. For example, if market price rises to $30, the firm supplies the quantity at point B, about 33 units. MC below A is not part of supply because the firm shuts down.
